title: AI
description: The models behind every AI feature, what may leave the platform, what it costs and the semantic index.

status.builtinBody: No data leaves the platform. Choose a chat model under Models to turn on generative answers.
status.maskingOn: Personal data is masked before a prompt leaves the platform.
status.maskingOff: Masking is off: prompts are sent to the provider as they are.
status.portableHint: Dev databases without pgvector; production images include it.
status.budgetSpent: Budget spent: AI calls are refused until next month

chat.title: Chat model
chat.description: Writes answers, summaries and triage suggestions. Without one, AI features run in builtin mode.

none.label: None
none.hint: Builtin mode: retrieval and templates only

anthropic.label: Anthropic (Claude)
anthropic.hint: Claude models through the Anthropic API

openaiCompatible.label: OpenAI-compatible
openaiCompatible.hint: OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio and others

chat.noneNote: AI features answer from the knowledge base and similar tickets, and fill in templates. No prompt leaves the platform.
chat.modelHintAnthropic: Leave empty to use the default model, {model}.
chat.modelHintOpenai: The model or deployment name exactly as the endpoint expects it.
chat.priceHintKnown: Used to estimate cost. Leave empty to use the known price of the model.
chat.priceHintCustom: Used to estimate cost. Leave empty if the endpoint is free, such as a model you host yourself.
chat.baseUrlHintAnthropic: Only for a proxy or gateway in front of the Anthropic API. Leave empty to call Anthropic directly.
chat.baseUrlHintOpenai: The API root, ending before /chat/completions or /responses. Pick a preset to start from.

responses.label: Responses
responses.hint: /responses: OpenAI's newer API, also in Azure OpenAI, vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio and LiteLLM

embeddings.title: Embeddings
embeddings.description: Turn articles and tickets into vectors for semantic search and grounded answers.

builtin.label: Builtin
builtin.hint: Offline, 384 dimensions, every language, no key

openaiCompatible.label: OpenAI-compatible
openaiCompatible.hint: OpenAI, Voyage AI, Ollama and others

embeddings.builtinNote: The builtin embedder runs inside the platform: no key, no cost, and text never leaves it. External models usually find better matches for paraphrased questions.
embeddings.dimensionsHint: Leave empty for the model's native size. Only OpenAI's text-embedding-3 models can be shortened.
embeddings.priceHint: Used to estimate cost. Leave empty if the endpoint is free.
embeddings.reembedWarning: Changing the embedding model re-embeds all indexed documents in the background. Until it finishes, semantic search only finds the documents already re-embedded.

key.label: API key
key.willRemove: The key will be removed when you save.
key.hint: Stored encrypted and never shown again.
key.providerChanged: The stored key was saved for another provider, so it is removed when you save unless you enter a new one.
key.urlChanged: The stored key will be sent to the new address. Replace or remove it if it belongs to another service.

test.saveFirst: Save first: the test uses the saved settings.
test.nothingToTest: Builtin mode: there is no chat model to test.

validation.url: Enter an address that starts with http:// or https://.
validation.dimensions: Enter a whole number between 0 and 4,000.
validation.headerName: Use letters, digits and - only, for example X-Tenant-Id.
validation.headerReserved: The platform sets this header itself.
validation.headerValue: A header value can't contain line breaks.
validation.headerDuplicate: Each header can appear only once.

connection.title: Connection options
connection.headersHint: Sent with every request, for example a gateway's tenant or routing header. Values are stored encrypted and never shown again.
connection.insecureTlsHint: Only for a server on your own network with a self-signed certificate. Recorded in the audit log.
connection.insecureTlsWarning: Certificates are not checked: anyone who can intercept the connection can read prompts and replies. Prefer a certificate your servers trust.

masking.title: Masking
masking.description: Personal and secret data is replaced with placeholders before a prompt leaves the platform and restored in the reply, so the provider never sees the values.
masking.enabled: Mask data before it leaves the platform
masking.enabledHint: Applies to every call to an external chat model.
masking.offWarning: Masking is off: prompts, including any personal data in tickets and articles, are sent to the provider as they are.
masking.categoriesHint: Each example shows what the model receives.

phone.label: Phone numbers
phone.hint: 9 digits or more; dates and times are left alone.

card.label: Card numbers
card.hint: Luhn-checked, so order and ticket numbers stay.

id.label: National IDs
id.hint: TW ID, JP My Number, US SSN.

masking.customHint: One regular expression per line, such as an employee or asset number format. Matches become {placeholder}, and so on.

budget.title: Monthly budget
budget.description: A ceiling on what AI may cost each calendar month (UTC).
budget.label: Budget
budget.hint: 0 means no limit. Once this month's spend reaches the budget, AI calls are refused ({code}) until the next month.

validation.pattern: Line {line, number} isn't a valid regular expression.
validation.patternServer: One of the patterns isn't a valid regular expression.
validation.budget: Enter an amount between 0 and 1,000,000, with at most 2 decimals.

chart.description: Per day (UTC). Hover over or focus a day, then use the arrow keys, to read its values.
chart.label: {measure} per day, {from} to {to}
chart.empty: No AI calls in this period.

byFeature.title: By feature
byFeature.description: Which features call AI, and what they cost.
byFeature.empty: No AI calls in this period.

byModel.title: By model
byModel.empty: No model calls in this period.

recent.title: Recent calls
recent.description: The latest 50 calls, whatever the period.
recent.masked: {count, plural, one {# value masked} other {# values masked}}

store.title: Vector store
store.pgvectorBody: Vectors are stored with the pgvector extension and searched through an HNSW index, which stays fast as the index grows.
store.portableBody: This database has no pgvector extension, so vectors are stored as plain arrays and compared in SQL. Results are the same but searches slow down with many documents. Dev databases without pgvector use this mode; production images include it.

content.title: Indexed content
content.description: What semantic search and AI answers can draw on. Every chunk keeps the permissions of its source, so answers never reveal what a person couldn't open.
content.empty: Nothing is indexed yet. Articles and resolved tickets are added as they are published.
content.stale: {count, plural, =0 {Every document uses the current model.} one {# document still uses an older model.} other {# documents still use an older model.}}
content.reembedStarted: Re-embedding started. It runs in the background.

mcp.description: Claude Code, Claude Desktop and IDE agents can use ISBP over the Model Context Protocol, with the same permission checks and audit log as the assistant.
mcp.endpointHint: Requests from other websites are refused.
mcp.versionsBody: Requests that name revision 2026-07-28 are served statelessly; clients that start with initialize get 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18 or 2025-03-26.
mcp.accessBody: Only API clients holding {permission}, with their API key or an OAuth client-credentials token. Every call runs with the client’s own permissions and is recorded in the audit log.
mcp.clientsTitle: API clients that may use MCP
mcp.clientsEmpty: No API client may use MCP yet. Give one the permission in Administration → API clients.
mcp.offeredTools: Tools: everything the API client may do that can’t destroy data. Read-only tools are marked as such.
mcp.offeredResources: Settings: the settings it may change, with their current values and a guide, so an agent can propose changes.
mcp.offeredChangeSets: Changes become change sets: an agent proposes, and nothing is live until a person reviews and applies it in ISBP.
mcp.offeredNoDestructive: Destructive tools need a person’s confirmation in ISBP, so they aren’t offered.
mcp.connectBody: Run this command in a terminal, then replace the placeholder with the API key of a client that may use MCP.
mcp.placeholderHint: The key is a placeholder: never paste a real key into shared notes or chats.
mcp.transport: Transport: Streamable HTTP with JSON responses and no sessions.
mcp.naming: Tools are named module__tool. The settings an agent may change are listed under isbp://customizations, each with its schema, guide and objects.
